note: Narration source. 'at' = planned start (s) in the film; 'est' = estimated spoken length at ~2.6 words/s. After the real voiceover is generated, tools/build.py re-times from the measured clip lengths. 'tts' is what the voice engine reads (phonetic spelling of Lsir).

lines.text: And this is the same sentence, over a mobile phone line.
lines.tts: And this is the same sentence... over a mobile phone line.

lines.text: The best free Armenian model gets eleven of sixteen words wrong.
lines.tts: [serious] The best free Armenian model gets eleven of sixteen words wrong.

lines.text: Many older people in Armenia speak only Armenian. When clinics answer calls with voice assistants, these callers get misheard.
lines.tts: Many older people in Armenia speak only Armenian. When clinics answer calls with voice assistants... these callers get misheard.

lines.text: A phone line keeps only a narrow slice of the voice. Nobody had measured what that does to Armenian.
lines.tts: A phone line keeps only a narrow slice of the voice. Nobody had measured what that does to Armenian.

lines.text: We tested five free models on 932 test recordings. The default Whisper model that most apps use does worse than writing nothing at all.
lines.tts: We tested five free models on nine hundred thirty-two test recordings. The default Whisper model that most apps use... does worse than writing nothing at all.

lines.text: So we built Lsir: listen, in Armenian.
lines.tts: [warmly] So we built Luh-seer: listen, in Armenian.

lines.text: Pick a sentence, send it down a mobile line our model never trained on, and compare.
lines.tts: Pick a sentence, send it down a mobile line our model never trained on, and compare.

lines.text: The original model: eleven words wrong. Lsir: five. Both answer in about two seconds.
lines.tts: The original model: eleven words wrong. Luh-seer: five. Both answer in about two seconds.

lines.text: Lsir is that same model with a small adapter on the part that listens: one and a half percent of its weights, trained with half the clips sent through random phone lines.
lines.tts: Luh-seer is that same model with a small adapter on the part that listens: one and a half percent of its weights, trained with half the clips sent through random phone lines.

lines.text: On 932 test recordings over that unseen mobile codec, errors fall from 22.1 to 20.8 percent, and the gain holds on a second dataset.
lines.tts: On nine hundred thirty-two test recordings over that unseen mobile codec, errors fall from twenty-two point one to twenty point eight percent... and the gain holds on a second dataset.

lines.text: Next: real phone calls, and older voices. Public Armenian speech data has no one over 59.
lines.tts: [thoughtful] Next: real phone calls, and older voices. Public Armenian speech data has no one over fifty-nine.
